html:
On 16 November 2006 riots broke out in Nukuʻalofa, the capital of Tonga, after parliament delayed reforms that would give commoners more power. Much of the central business district was burned and several people died.

Many of the shops burned belonged to Chinese migrants and to businesses linked to the royal family and nobles. Troops and police from Australia and New Zealand helped restore order.

The riots pushed the monarchy to act. King George Tupou V gave up much of his power, and the elections of 2010 gave elected commoners a majority in parliament for the first time since the 1875 constitution. The pro-democracy leader ʻAkilisi Pohiva later became prime minister.
sum: On 16 November 2006 riots broke out in Nukuʻalofa, the capital of Tonga, after parliament delayed reforms that would give commoners more power. Much of the central business district was burned and several people died.
